statement: Do not rely on a balance's built-in auto-calibration alone; also carry out external performance checks.
quote: The auto-calibration feature of a balance may not be relied upon to the exclusion of an external performance check (21 CFR 211.68).

statement: For scales with a built-in auto-calibrator, perform external performance checks periodically; these may be less frequent than for scales without that feature.
quote: For a scale with a built-in auto-calibrator, we recommend that external performance checks be performed on a periodic basis, but less frequently as compared to a scale without this feature.

statement: Set the frequency of balance performance checks according to how often the scale is used and how critical the process or analytical step is and its tolerance.
quote: The frequency of performance checks depends on the frequency of use of the scale and the criticality and tolerance of the process or analytical step.

statement: Verify the calibration of a balance's auto-calibrator periodically (commonly once a year) using NIST-traceable standards or nationally accredited equivalents used in other countries.
quote: the calibration of an auto-calibrator should be periodically verified—a common frequency is once a year—using National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-traceable standards or NIST-accredited standards in use in other countries.

statement: Firms may choose the equipment that best fits their needs, provided it can meet the relevant CGMP requirements.
quote: Firms are afforded the flexibility to select equipment that best satisfies their particular needs and that is capable of meeting the relevant CGMP requirements.

statement: Select all equipment used in the manufacturing process so that it produces quality products in line with CGMP.
quote: Each firm is responsible for selecting all equipment used in their manufacturing process to produce quality products in accordance with CGMP.

statement: Define the appropriate intended use for each piece of equipment's operation.
quote: They are also responsible for selecting the appropriate intended use for the equipment's operation

statement: Firms may modify standard equipment designs to suit their process, as long as the modified equipment is compatible with the product being processed.
quote: are free to modify standard equipment designs to best suit their process and that are compatible with the product under process.

statement: Equipment must be of a design suitable for its intended operations and for cleaning and maintenance.
quote: The CGMP regulations require that equipment be of appropriate design to facilitate operations for its intended use and for cleaning and maintenance (see 21 CFR 211.63 and 211.67)

statement: Equipment surfaces that contact components, in-process materials or drug products must not be reactive, additive or absorptive to an extent that changes the product's safety, identity, strength, quality or purity beyond official or other established requirements.
quote: that any equipment surface in contact with components, in-process materials, or drug products not be reactive, additive, or absorptive so as to "alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements" (see 21 CFR 211.65).

statement: Total organic carbon (or total carbon) testing may be used for routine residue monitoring and for cleaning validation.
quote: TOC or TC can be an acceptable method for monitoring residues routinely and for cleaning validation.

statement: Before relying on TOC, establish that a substantial amount of the contaminating material is organic and contains carbon that can be oxidised under the TOC test conditions.
quote: In order for TOC to be functionally suitable, it should first be established that a substantial amount of the contaminating material(s) is organic and contains carbon that can be oxidized under TOC test conditions.

statement: TOC may be used, where justified, for both direct surface samples and indirect rinse-water samples.
quote: TOC use may be justified for direct surface sample testing as well as indirect (rinse water) sample testing.

statement: When using TOC, attribute all detected carbon to the target compound(s) when comparing results against the established limit.
quote: any detected carbon is to be attributed to the target compound(s) for comparing with the established limit.

statement: When using TOC, keep carbon from sources other than the contaminant being removed as low as possible.
quote: Thus, a firm should limit background carbon (i.e., carbon from sources other than the contaminant being removed) as much as possible.

statement: Correct the established TOC limit, or the detected residue amount compared with the specification, for the carbon content of the target material.
quote: The established limit, or the amount of residue detected for comparison to the specification, should correct for the target material’s composition of carbon.

statement: Perform recovery studies for the residue sampling and test method, as for any cleaning method.
quote: As for any cleaning method, recovery studies are necessary (21 CFR 211.160(b)).

statement: If TOC samples are held for long periods before analysis, verify how the holding time affects accuracy and limit of quantitation.
quote: If TOC samples are being held for long periods of time before analysis, a firm should verify the impact of sample holding time on accuracy and limit of quantitation.
condition: TOC samples held long before analysis

statement: When monitoring the environment for Mycoplasma, use selective media such as PPLO broth or agar.
quote: Environmental monitoring of Mycoplasma requires selective media (PPLO broth or agar).

statement: Identify drugs that pose cross-contamination risks (such as potent compounds) and define the controls needed to eliminate the risk of cross-contamination in non-dedicated equipment and facilities, including proper cleaning, cleaning validation and other contaminant controls.
quote: However, manufacturers should identify drugs with such risks and define the controls necessary to eliminate risk of product cross-contamination in nondedicated equipment and facilities. Such controls include proper cleaning, cleaning validation, and other contaminant controls.

statement: Validate that cleaning procedures are adequate to ensure cross-contamination does not occur.
quote: Firms must validate that cleaning procedures are adequate to ensure that cross-contamination does not occur.

statement: When designing a facility, evaluate manufacturing processes carefully to choose procedural controls and a floor plan that optimise the flow of materials, equipment and people to help prevent product contamination.
quote: In designing a facility, firms should carefully evaluate manufacturing processes to determine the best procedural controls and floor plan—optimizing the flow of materials, equipment, and people—to help prevent product contamination.

statement: Clean and maintain all equipment, dedicated or multipurpose, and sanitise and/or sterilise it as appropriate to the nature of the drug, at appropriate intervals, to prevent malfunctions or contamination that would change the product's safety, identity, strength, quality or purity beyond official or other established requirements.
quote: 21 CFR 211.67(a) requires that any equipment, including dedicated and multipurpose equipment, is “cleaned, maintained, and, as appropriate for the nature of the drug, sanitized and/or sterilized at appropriate intervals to prevent malfunctions or contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements.”

statement: Ensure residues (for example active ingredients and cleaning agents) are adequately removed from product contact surfaces of all equipment at product changeovers and/or between production campaigns, depending on the materials and surfaces involved.
quote: You must therefore ensure that residues (e.g., active ingredients, cleaning agents) are adequately removed from product contact surfaces of all equipment during product changeovers and/or between production campaigns, depending on the types of materials and surfaces in use.

statement: Document cleaning procedures well and keep them consistent for their intended use.
quote: Cleaning procedures should be well-documented and consistent for their intended use.

statement: Design the cleaning validation program to give assurance that residues are effectively removed from product contact surfaces.
quote: Cleaning validation programs should provide assurance that residues are effectively removed from product contact surfaces,

statement: Choose test methods that demonstrate the effectiveness of residue removal.
quote: manufacturers should select test methods that demonstrate their effectiveness.

statement: Consult guidelines from trade and professional associations (for example ISPE or PDA) for additional information on conducting cleaning validation.
quote: does recommend consulting guidelines published by various trade and professional associations for additional information (e.g., International Society for Pharmaceutical Engineering, Parenteral Drug Association).

statement: Clean equipment to prevent contamination that would change the product's safety, identity, strength, quality or purity beyond official or other established requirements.
quote: CGMP regulations require that equipment be cleaned to prevent contamination that “would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements” (see 21 CFR 211.67).

statement: Clean equipment as thoroughly as can reasonably be achieved, to a residue limit documented as safe, that raises no product quality concerns and that leaves no visible residue.
quote: Equipment should be as clean as can be reasonably achieved to a residue limit that is documented to be safe, causes no product quality concerns, and leaves no visible residues.

statement: Remove all contamination that is reasonably avoidable and removable; leaving it is never acceptable.
quote: Contamination that is reasonably avoidable and removable is never considered acceptable.

statement: Validate proposed cleaning procedures as they will be used routinely.
quote: Firms must, however, ensure that they validate proposed cleaning procedures as for routine use

statement: During cleaning validation, do not pre-clean or otherwise make it easier for the procedures under validation to meet their cleaning objectives.
quote: should not pre-clean or otherwise attempt to make it easier for the procedures being validated to meet their cleaning objectives.

statement: Manufacture the material being cleaned at a similar scale and in a similar manner as during validation.
quote: The material being cleaned should be manufactured at a similar scale and manner as during validation.

statement: Where equipment is stored uncleaned for longer than the validated time, sample it to show the cleaning procedures remain effective.
quote: Also, firms should sample equipment that is stored uncleaned for a longer time than validated to demonstrate that their cleaning procedures are effective.

statement: Run a residue-monitoring program whose frequency and methods are set by risk assessment.
quote: However, a residue-monitoring program whose frequency and methods have been determined by risk assessment is recommended.

statement: Keep laboratory glassware clean.
quote: Glassware must, of course, be clean,

statement: Laboratory cleaning procedures may consist of repeated rinses with the solvent used to prepare the analyte, followed by oven drying.
quote: Laboratory cleaning procedures may include repetitive rinses with the solvent used to prepare the analyte, followed by oven drying.

statement: For particularly sensitive analyses or difficult-to-clean compounds, a firm may sample its glassware for residual contamination to rule out or investigate possible interference.
quote: A firm may elect to sample its glassware for residual contamination to exclude or explore the possibility of interference in the case of particularly sensitive analyses or difficult-to-clean compounds.
condition: particularly sensitive analyses or difficult-to-clean compounds

statement: Do not use contaminated laboratory equipment as a frequent excuse to reject or discard aberrant results.
quote: Contaminated laboratory equipment, however, should not be a frequent excuse for rejecting or discarding aberrant results.

statement: Maintain laboratory equipment in a clean and sanitary condition so analytical results can be relied on.
quote: We expect firms to maintain laboratory equipment in a clean and sanitary manner to provide confidence in the analytical results.

statement: Establish acceptance limits for detergent residues and be ready to give FDA the basis for those limits.
quote: It is the firm’s responsibility to establish acceptance limits and to be prepared to provide the basis for those limits to FDA.

statement: Detergent residues must not exceed their established acceptance limits.
quote: Residues must not exceed their established acceptance limits

statement: Detergent residues must not adversely affect the drug product's safety, efficacy, quality or stability.
quote: must not adversely alter drug product safety, efficacy, quality, or stability

statement: When setting up a cleaning procedure for a specific piece of equipment, take into account its material of construction, its exact design, how it is used, and especially the specific substances that could contaminate it; do not apply a cleaning procedure validated for one material to other equipment or compounds without this.
quote: In establishing an effective cleaning procedure for a particular piece of equipment, firms must consider its material of construction/fabrication, exact design, conditions of use, and, in particular, the specific substances that could contaminate the equipment.
condition: when establishing a cleaning procedure for a given piece of equipment

statement: Hold data covering material of construction, exact design, conditions of use and the specific potential contaminants to demonstrate that a given piece of equipment is cleaned effectively.
quote: Therefore, to demonstrate proof of cleaning for a given piece of equipment, firms should have data that relate to all of these factors.
condition: to demonstrate proof of cleaning for a given piece of equipment

statement: In cleaning validation, do not rely on rinse samples alone; also measure residue or contaminant on the equipment surface by a direct method, if feasible.
quote: For cleaning validation, rinse samples alone would not be acceptable; firms should also measure the residue or contaminant on the equipment surface using a direct method (if feasible).
condition: if a direct method is feasible

statement: Swab and rinse samples may both be used during cleaning validation, provided the rinse solvent has been shown to dissolve the residues of concern and is otherwise suitable for use on the surfaces being sampled.
quote: some firms use both swab and rinse samples during the course of their cleaning validation. This is acceptable if the rinse solvent has been demonstrated to dissolve residues of concern and is otherwise suitable for use on the surfaces to be sampled.
condition: if the rinse solvent is shown to dissolve residues of concern and suit the surfaces

statement: After cleaning validation, run a residue-monitoring program for routine equipment cleaning, with frequency and methods set by risk assessment, to show the validated process keeps cleaning the equipment consistently.
quote: For routine equipment cleaning after validation, a residue-monitoring program whose frequency and methods have been determined by risk assessment is recommended to demonstrate that the validated process continues to consistently clean the equipment.
condition: for routine equipment cleaning after validation

statement: Use scientifically sound sampling and analytical test methods for cleaning validation that give adequate scientific rationale to support the validation.
quote: the sampling and analytical test methods should be scientifically sound and should provide adequate scientific rationale to support the validation.

statement: Make sure whatever material is chosen for the water for injection system is suitable for its intended use.
quote: Whatever material a firm selects for its WFI system must be suitable for its intended use.
condition: for a water for injection system

statement: Make sure the materials chosen for virtually all production equipment are suitable for their intended use.
quote: Whatever material a firm selects for its WFI system must be suitable for its intended use. This holds true for virtually all production equipment.

statement: When assessing whether water for injection system piping is suitable, take into account the surface texture or finish of the interior wall (e.g., smoothness, waviness), its resistance to high temperatures and pressures, and its ability to withstand sterilizing and sanitizing agents and procedures.
quote: When evaluating the suitability of a WFI system’s piping, consider the surface texture or finish of the piping’s interior wall (e.g., smoothness, waviness), its ability to resist high temperatures and pressures, and its ability to withstand sterilizing and sanitizing agents and procedures.
condition: when evaluating suitability of WFI system piping

statement: Ensure equipment surfaces that contact components, in-process materials or drug products are not reactive, additive or absorptive so as to alter the product's safety, identity, strength, quality or purity beyond its official or established requirements.
quote: Equipment surfaces that are in contact with components, in-process materials, or drug products must not be reactive, additive, or absorptive so as to alter the drug product’s safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity beyond its official or established requirements.
condition: surfaces in contact with components, in-process materials or drug products
